correctness.rationale: Reconstructed KG(5,2) vertices as ten 2-subsets and edges as disjointness. Any proper 3-colouring uses a unique four-member independent colour class, which must be a star, and complementary size-three star/triangle classes. These give 5*4=20 ordered-pair palette-free labels with six colour-name assignments each. For each labelled state the six Kempe flips are precisely whole connected bichromatic components; the combinatorial quotient adjacency sends (i,j) to (i,k) for k distinct from i,j, or to (j,i). Thus the palette quotient is the line graph of once-subdivided K5, with 20 vertices and 40 edges. Independently generated all 120 colourings, all 360 undirected Kempe edges, and ran exhaustive all-source BFS from every state: labelled shells (1,6,25,61,27), quotient shells (1,4,6,9), diameters 4 and 3 respectively. This is exhaustive finite verification and a structural argument, not a sampled conjecture.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns exactly proper vertex 3-colourings with named colours and single-component two-colour Kempe changes; not edge colourings, equitable/perfect 3-colourings, or other recolouring adjacencies.
